Cook's era as Apple CEO is numbered, with John Ternus set to officially take the top job on September 1. Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan believes Ternus could usher in a bolder, more risk-tolerant era for Apple.

John Ternus is expected to make bigger bets on new products, acquisitions, and research and development once he takes over as CEO.

The Apple CEO transition is nearly complete. So far, the company has worked hard to emphasize the continuity Ternus will bring to the role.

However, not everyone on Wall Street is convinced Ternus will follow in Cook's footsteps.

Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan reiterated a strong "Buy" rating on Apple in a research note obtained by The Street. One of the key reasons the bank supports Apple is the expectation that Ternus will continue Cook's legacy while having a greater "risk appetite." Here's what Moaz Farouk wrote:

The bank highlighted Apple's move to abandon its "net cash neutral" goal as an early signal that management may be more willing to deploy capital. This would mean more R&D spending, more capital expenditures, and potentially larger acquisitions — areas that were not a focus of Cook-era strategy. Bank of America believes Apple under Ternus could move more quickly into entirely new product categories, including AI glasses, AirPods with cameras, smart rings, smart home, personal assistants, and robotics.

Ultimately, Bank of America believes Ternus will continue Cook's legacy of building Apple into a high-margin global machine, but expects him to leverage the company's existing strengths to make bolder bets in the future.

We may not see any major changes at the start of Ternus' tenure as CEO. But over the coming months, any potential shifts in priorities could gradually come into focus.

What are your expectations for John Ternus as Apple's new CEO? Let us know in the comments.
